title: Budget Alert Simulations & Rate Limit Playbook - QBR Worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a working worksheet for Customer Success QBR prep that lets us: simulate forward token spend, model rate-limit impacts, define alert thresholds, and prepare renewal talking points around spend predictability. Intended for CS leads + account finance when prepping QBR decks.

How to use (quick):
1) Pull last 90 days token-by-route and per-model cost per 1k tokens from billing API.
2) Populate the "raw usage" sheet (tokens, requests, model, route, timestamp, seat count).
3) Run the scenario blocks below to generate 3 forecast lines for the QBR slides: baseline (trend), conservative (p75 spike), aggressive (p95 spike / model upgrade).
4) Copy the metric bullets under "QBR talking points" into the QBR slide export.

Key metrics (definitions):
- Token Spend: raw input tokens * cost-per-1k-token (USD).
- Velocity (tokens/min): rolling median of tokens/minute over last 24h per route.
- Token Efficiency Ratio (TER): tokens / app-action (higher = less efficient prompts).
- Spend Velocity Normalized (SVN): tokens/day / active-seat or tokens/day / DAU (choose one for the account).
- Rate Limit Cushion: configured rate limit / 99th pct observed RPS.

Data sources (typical):
- Billing API: per-model cost and invoice rollups.
- Usage logs: streaming events with route tag, model id, tokens_in, tokens_out.
- Account metadata: active-seat counts, product tiers, renewal dates.

Baseline calculations (formula snippets you can drop into a sheet):
- avg_tokens_per_request = sum(tokens) / count(requests)
- daily_tokens = sum(tokens where date = X)
- projected_monthly_spend = (avg_daily_tokens * 30) * (cost_per_1k_tokens / 1000)
- normalized_spend_by_seat = projected_monthly_spend / active_seats

Simulation scenarios (what to run before the QBR):
Scenario A - Baseline trend:
- fit simple 14-day linear trend to daily_tokens, project 30 days.
- assume model mix constant.

Scenario B - Usage spike / marketing event (p75):
- take baseline, add 40% random single-day spikes on top of baseline for 3 days in the next 30-day window.

Scenario C - Model upgrade cost regression (p95):
- assume new model deployed increases tokens per request by +25% and cost-per-1k increases by 10% (or substitute actual contract model).

Monte Carlo bucket (optional, recommended for large accounts):
- run 1000 draws where daily uplift ~ Normal(mu=0.05, sigma=0.12), apply occasional heavy day (5% of draws add +150% for a single day).
- capture distribution of monthly spend (p50/p75/p90/p99) and include ranges in QBR.

Quick example (numbers to paste into slides):
- last 30d avg daily tokens = 45,000,000
- cost per 1k tokens = $0.80
- baseline monthly = 45,000,000 * 30 * 0.0008 = $1,080,000
- p75 spike monthly = baseline * 1.35 ≈ $1,458,000
- model-upgrade monthly = baseline * 1.35 * 1.10 ≈ $1,603,800

Suggested alert thresholds and actions (client-facing, concise):
- Informational (60% of committed budget or 70% of expected monthly run rate): send monthly QBR note + run optimization checklist.
- Warning (80%): CS + FinOps notified, schedule 15-min sync to review mitigation (caching, quantization, batching, route-level throttles).
- Critical (95% or sudden daily > 200% of avg): automatic rate-limit fallback -> apply temporary global throttle to non-critical routes, page on-call SRE if no rapid mitigation.

Rate-limit playbook (stepwise):
1) Detect: threshold-crossing event, attach last 24h top-10 routes by tokens.
2) Quick triage (CS lead): check for product launch, marketing push, spike in DAU, or bug.
3) Immediate soft actions (within 5 min): enable route-specific 429 policy, increase token-cache TTL where applicable, apply short fixed window throttle for exploratory routes.
4) Mid-term (30-90 min): move heavy traffic to cheaper model variant (if available), enable batching on compatible routes, patch prompt templates if runaway tokens per request.
5) Escalation (if >2 hrs and spend still high): open a billing hold with customer (if contractual), execute negotiated temporary cap with commit to increased capacity.

QBR slide-ready sections (copy / paste):
- 1-line summary: "This period the account ran at X% of committed capacity; expected burn next 30d = $Y (p75 $Z)."
- Key drivers: model mix shift / new route / marketing event / growth in free-tier users.
- Recommendations: apply route-level cache, consider Dedicated pool or committed discount, add guardrails for new feature launches.

Prep checklist for CS lead (items to complete 48h before QBR):
- [ ] Export last 90 days raw usage (model, tokens_in/out, route).
- [ ] Calculate TER by route and flag top 5 inefficient flows.
- [ ] Run p75/p95 simulations and drop graphs into slides.
- [ ] Confirm renewal date and current committed spend.
- [ ] Draft 3 renewal levers tailored to customer (discount tiers, dedicated capacity commitment, optimize/observe package).

Sample column layout for the sheet (copy to new sheet tab):
Date | Route | Model | Requests | Tokens_in | Tokens_out | Cost_per_1k | Daily_tokens | Active_seats | Notes
2025-10-12 | /chat/send | rw-instruct-v1 | 45,123 | 3,200,500 | 1,120,345 | 0.80 | 4,320,845 | 210 | marketing push

Notes to self / open questions (to resolve with Eng/FinOps):
- How accurate is cost_per_1k in hourly billing when model variants are autoswitched? Use weighted-average cost across the hour.
- Should we standardize on SVN by DAU or by seats for enterprise vs startup accounts?
- Add a templated SHELL script to fetch per-route 1m rollups from billing API (Evan to add).

Slack escalation snippet (short):
@here Account X hitting 92% of monthly projection (p99 daily spike). Top routes: /chat/send (48%), /embed/query (22%). CS lead Maya T. triaging. Suggested immediate action: enable route throttle for /chat/send and flip to cheaper model variant for embed calls.

Renewal conversation bullets (for QBR):
- "We saw a p75 scenario that would take you ~X% above current committed levels — options: apply committed capacity, or adopt route-level throttles + Optimize audit (free 2-week pilot)."
- "Tradeoffs: Dedicated reduces per-token cost and improves predictability; Optimize will likely reduce spend by Y% within 30 days for most chat-heavy workflows."

Appendix: quick optimization checklist (one-liners):
- prefix caching for repeated prompts
- static prompt deduping and template compression
- session KV caching to reduce repeated context tokens
- consider 8-bit quantized model variant for high-volume non-critical routes

End of worksheet.

-- Maya (notes: keep one copy with raw exports attached, update the Monte Carlo params per account size)
